raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The progression from a relatively normal chest X-ray (Figure 2) to CT scans showing a large right pleural effusion (Figure 1a) and extensive mediastinal gas/abscess (Figure 1b) indicates worsening pathology consistent with an aorto-esophageal fistula. The development of air pockets in the mediastinum and increasing pleural fluid are hallmark signs of esophageal perforation and subsequent mediastinitis.
